title: 5 Things AI Still Can’t Do for UX Research
intro: AI can automate research activities. It can't yet produce trustworthy findings on its own.

topics.title: 5 Things AI Still Can’t Do for UX Research

learn.title: The five gaps
learn.text:
**1. Replace real users** — synthetic users sound human and confirm what you already believe
**2. Design good research questions** — knowing when to add context, probe or steer is judgement
**3. Model complex interactions** — see below
**4. Choose the right statistics** — running code isn't choosing a test
**5. Interpret results against the decision** — the finding has to answer a specific question

try.q: Which gap is “running code isn't the same as choosing a test”?
try.explain: The calculation is easy; the choice is the expertise.

learn.title: The GOMS-KLM experiment
learn.text:
Calabro gave a model his operator table, the workflows and screenshots, and asked for a GOMS-KLM analysis.

It **missed operators, misread interface elements and invented interactions**.

Fixing the output took about **six times longer** than doing the analysis by hand.

*Newer models may do better — the specific result is tied to the model of the day.*

try.q: What made the AI's GOMS-KLM output expensive?
options: Checking and correcting it took longer than doing it
It refused to complete the analysis without more detail
It required a paid model tier
try.explain: About six times the manual effort.

learn.title: Where prompting habits hurt
learn.text:
Habits from writing neutral prompts can **strip out the context a good research question needs**.

A research question often needs a scenario, a moment in time, or a deliberate frame — the opposite of a clean, context-free prompt.

That's the same point as the interview-questions article: neutrality is a tool, not the goal.

try.q: How can prompt-writing habits damage a research question?
options: They remove context the question needs
They introduce subtly leading language into probes
try.explain: Clean and context-free produces flat answers.

test.q: What can AI do well here?
Why can't synthetic users surprise you?
options: They confirm what you already believe
They are too slow to respond
They lack demographic diversity in their answers
test.explain: And surprise is where the best findings come from.

test.q: What did the model get wrong in the GOMS-KLM test?
options: It missed operators and invented interactions
It used the wrong operator times
It refused to work from the screenshots provided
test.explain: Given the operator table, workflows and screenshots.
A finding only matters in relation to a specific choice.

test.q: How should the six-times figure be read today?
options: As tied to the model of the day
As applying to every kind of AI analysis
test.explain: Newer models may do better; the five gaps are the durable part.
